title: Lamb Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
subtitle: Moroccan slow-braised lamb with aromatic spices
excerpt: The definitive Moroccan tagine: lamb shoulder slow-braised in a clay pot with preserved lemon, green olives, cumin, ginger, and saffron until it falls apart in the sweet, intensely aromatic sauce. Served piled over couscous.

recipe.sourceNotes: The tagine is both the vessel (a distinctive conical clay pot from North Africa) and the slow-braised stew cooked within it. The Moroccan lamb tagine with preserved lemon and olives (mrouzia) is among the best-known preparations, combining the characteristic Moroccan flavour palette of warm spices (cumin, ginger, coriander, cinnamon), saffron, and preserved lemon with the briny sharpness of green olives. Preserved lemons, made by salting and packing fresh lemons in lemon juice for several weeks, are an essential North African ingredient and cannot be substituted with fresh lemon; the flavour is fermented, soft-rinded, and deeply citrus. A tagine may be used; a heavy casserole with a tight lid works just as well.

content.text: Brown the lamb well before braising; the colour and flavour from the Maillard reaction are essential. Only use the skin of the preserved lemon, not the flesh, which is very bitter. The green olives go in only in the final 20 minutes so they keep their texture. Taste the sauce before serving; preserved lemons vary considerably in saltiness and you may need to add very little extra salt.

items.preparation: bone-in or boneless; cut into large chunks

content.text: Brown the lamb in batches in the oil over high heat. Set aside. Cook the onion in the same pot for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, ginger, and all the ground spices. Stir for 1 minute.
Return the lamb. Add the saffron with its water and 300 ml of water. Season. Cover and cook over the lowest possible heat for 1 hour 30 minutes, turning the lamb occasionally.

Add the preserved lemon and green olives. Simmer uncovered for a further 20 minutes until the sauce has reduced and the lamb is very tender. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve with couscous and scattered with fresh coriander.
